item.title: Republicans fail to ease one of Trump's greatest fears as Supreme Court measure collapses
item.description: House Democrats blocked a constitutional amendment to cap Supreme Court justices at nine after President Donald Trump warned of future court packing.
item.content:encoded:
House Democrats are nuking Republicans' effort to assuage one of President Donald Trump's biggest concerns about the future of the federal government.

A vote on a constitutional amendment to cap the number of Supreme Court justices failed on Wednesday afternoon after the vast majority of Democrats voted against it.

Trump has warned for months that he believes Democrats would seek to expand the Supreme Court if they took back control of Congress — something affirmed by top progressives, including former Vice President Kamala Harris and Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass.

House GOP leaders sought to head that off with a proposed amendment led by Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., that would mandate that just nine justices can sit on the high court.

KAMALA HARRIS BACKS MAJOR CHANGES TO THE SUPREME COURT, ELECTORAL COLLEGE AHEAD OF POSSIBLE 2028 CAMPAIGN

Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., opted to fast-track the legislation past multiple procedural hurdles in exchange for raising the threshold for passage from a simple majority to two-thirds, a maneuver known as "suspending the rules." But it failed to clinch that number, even though the majority of House lawmakers supported the amendment.

The U.S. Constitution allows Congress to set the number of seats on the Supreme Court bench, which is currently occupied by eight justices and one chief justice.

However, the Constitution itself does not dictate how many justices can exist. Republicans argued that changing that could make it much harder for a Democrat government to pack the court in the future in order to stack the judicial odds in its favor.

CARVILLE TELLS DEMS TO QUIETLY PREPARE POWER GRAB WITH DC, PUERTO RICO STATEHOOD AND SUPREME COURT PACKING

"Here's the question every American should ask: if a sitting majority can change the size of the Supreme Court the moment it dislikes rulings, what happens to the next time the other side is in power?" Biggs posed on Wednesday. "Once you go down that road, the court stops being an independent check on government power. It becomes another political institution controlled by whoever happens to hold the majority."

Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., among the progressives calling to increase the number of justices to 13, argued that Congress has changed the number of Supreme Court justices multiple times throughout history and dismissed the current tally as arbitrary.

"MAGA's proposal is to strip Congress of all authority in the matter, to freeze it, and cemented permanently in the constitutional architecture for all time with the suddenly magic number nine," Raskin said.

"It's another partisan power grab by MAGA, our colleagues, who fear for the results of the November election as their policies have brought us nothing but war, inflation, corruption, lawlessness and a $40 trillion debt — one quarter of it's supplied by this presidential administration. So the MAGA party wants to cement into place a profoundly partisan and lopsided...court that was gerrymandered and engineered by Mitch McConnell."

HARRIS LABELED 'INSTITUTIONAL ARSONIST' FOR PLAN TO FUNDAMENTALLY TRANSFORM SCOTUS AND ELECTORAL COLLEGE

He was referring to former Senate GOP Leader Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., and his critical role in helping secure the current conservative majority on the high court.

Progressives have argued that expanding the court to 13 would mean there is one justice for every federal circuit court.

Rep. Mark Harris, R-N.C., attacked the left's push as an effort to seize political power.

"For decades, we have heard calls from those unhappy with the ideological balance of the Supreme Court to pack the court. The alarming rise of such calls should worry all of us, because their objective is not to uphold ethical principles or even to protect individual rights, but rather to consolidate power and intimidate the court," Harris said.

Later, Rep. Mary Gay Scanlon, D-Pa., said that locking the number at nine would only extend the current conservative majority's power.

"I think it would be a grave mistake to dictate how many justices should sit on the Supreme Court in perpetuity, and thereby lock in for a generation or more a right-wing majority, which is engaged in an unprecedented assault on Supreme Court norms and our constitutional order for the past several years," Scanlon said.

item.title: DAVID MARCUS: Canada sees Trump trade war as ‘life and death’ while Americans barely notice
item.description: Expert Gary Mar warns Canada faces bigger sticks in a tariff battle with the United States as the Sept. 7 trade deal deadline approaches fast.
item.content:encoded:
Gary Mar is a guy who knows a thing or two about trade between the United States and Canada. As the president of the Canada West Foundation and a former minister dealing with trade for the Province of Alberta, he’s seen a lot — but nothing quite like the current asymmetrical trade dispute between the two nations.

America and our neighbors to the north face a Sept. 7 deadline to reach a new trade deal, or see crippling sanctions go into effect on both sides. But the citizens of each country are not treating this looming crisis the same way at all.

"The 49th parallel [is] like a two-way mirror," Mar told Fox News Digital this week. "Canadians look through it, and they see Americans. But Americans look at the same mirror, and they see themselves. So we get much more information on what’s going on in the United States than Americans ever get ... with respect to Canada."

CANADIAN PM TELLS TRUMP TO 'STOP TRYING TO BE TOUGH' IN TRADE FIGHT

This is a fair assessment. For example, most Americans likely do not know that, since President Donald Trump took office, Canadian grocery stores and pharmacies have aggressive signs pointing out what products were made in America, to boycott them. Nothing remotely like that has happened stateside.

Likewise, in the Great White North, these trade flare-ups are by far the biggest story in the country, fueled by a state-run media that might even hate Trump more than our domestic liberal media does. In America, this story is lucky to hit the C-slot of a cable news show.

‘CAPTAIN CANADA’ FIREBRAND UNLOADS ON TRUMP WITH PROFANE ONE-LINER AS TRADE WAR ESCALATES

The point is that, from the perspective of public opinion intensity, there is just no comparison. Canadians think they are in an existential fight, while most Americans barely know it is happening.

This asymmetry also applies to the political realities facing Trump and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.

Trump faces some Democrats all but siding with Canada. Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, for instance, said this week, "If you start a trade war with Canada, you are the a------."

FOX NEWS POLL: A SENATE BATTLE LOOMS IN MICHIGAN

I asked Mar if this kind of thing could happen in Canada — could conservative politicians like Pierre Poilievre come out in favor of Trump — and not surprisingly, the answer is no.

Speaking on the Canadian right, Mar said, "They can be critical of how the liberal government is conducting their relationship with the U.S., but it would be very difficult for the conservatives to say, ‘We agree with Donald Trump.’"

TRUMP TRADE CHIEF WARNS CANADA WALKED AWAY FROM 'THE BEST DEAL' TO TRIGGER 50% U.S. TARIFFS

It is reasonable to assume that this rally-round-the-maple-leaf moment of unity in Canada accrues to Carney’s benefit in negotiations, and Mar acknowledges that. As former House Speaker Newt Gingrich has suggested, Carney may be trying to game the U.S. midterms by punishing swing states like Maine and Michigan economically via tariffs.

But not everything is slanted against Trump in these negotiations. The biggest asymmetry of all is the sheer power of the U.S. economy, and Mar had some sobering words for Canada regarding an all-out tariff battle.

TRUMP'S CANADA TARIFF FIGHT REACHES CRITICAL POINT AS HOUSE GOP SUMMONS TRADE CHIEF

"What I see now is a discussion of who can inflict more pain on the other side," Mar said. "The difficulty for Canada getting involved in a tit-for-tat, or a stick-swinging incident — as we might use the metaphor from hockey — is that [the] U.S. has more sticks to swing. They’ve got bigger sticks to swing, and their sticks have spikes on them."

That about sums it up.

A POPULAR COCKTAIL HAS A TRUMP TRADE PROBLEM YOU PROBABLY DIDN’T KNOW ABOUT

Both Canada and the United States have good reasons to just make a deal by the upcoming deadline and put this all behind them, at least for now. But with each side blaming the other for the breakdown in talks, it may be too heavy a lift.

If talks fail, the real question won’t be how it impacts the midterms, but rather, whether it leads Canada to lean more heavily on other partners such as China, and whether Venezuela can actually be stable enough to attract oil companies away from friendly, old Canada.

Trump has a few more years to try to perfect his trade regime with our northern neighbor, and there will be bumps along the road. Americans should remember that for us, the trade battle may be a matter of minor national pride, but in Canada, it is absolutely life and death.

How that asymmetry finds its solution, may well tell the tale of the conflict’s end.

item.title: Obama-appointed judge ripped for blocking Trump mail-ballot rule: 'Run out the clock'
item.description: Judge Indira Talwani blocked new USPS mail-ballot rules just days before North Carolina begins mailing absentee ballots for 2026 midterms.
item.content:encoded:
An Obama-appointed federal judge is being branded an "activist" after she again blocked new U.S. Postal Service (USPS) mail-ballot requirements ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani issued a 14-day temporary restraining order last week blocking key portions of a new USPS policy governing the mailing of outbound ballots. The rule, developed in response to an executive order from President Donald Trump, would require election officials to submit ballot-envelope designs for approval and upload voter information and unique tracking barc

odes to a new USPS portal.

Jason Snead, executive director of the Honest Election Project, accused Talwani of trying to "run out the clock," arguing that the continued litigation could prevent the rule from taking effect before states begin mailing ballots for the midterms.

"Because of the antics of the left in this case, it’s very possible that we will not be able to get this rule put in place for the 2026 midterms," Snead told Fox News Digital. "Ballots do go out in just a couple of days, and I think, to a certain extent, their campaign to run out the clock may have succeeded."

MAIL-VOTING CRACKDOWN MOVES AHEAD AS TRUMP COURT WIN OPENS DOOR TO FEDERAL ACTION

North Carolina county election boards are scheduled to begin mailing absentee ballots Friday. Snead and Gregory Teufel, founder of OGC Law, LLC, both noted that election officials in the state had already taken steps toward complying with the USPS requirements.

Talwani found that the states lacked the time and money to redesign ballot envelopes, obtain USPS approval, modify election-management systems, train officials to use the new portal and upload voter information before the midterms. She concluded that compliance was "practically impossible" for the approaching election and warned that eligible voters could be disenfranchised.

Snead pushed back on that conclusion, arguing that the rule puts longstanding USPS recommendations into mandatory requirements.

"It’s a fairly straightforward rule," Snead said. "It’s largely premised on best practices that are already in place and gathering data that states already possess. The burdens are extraordinarily minimal as far as compliance is concerned, and the Postal Service is really just trying to better regulate the mail—not attempt to seize control of elections or to take away fundamental constitutional questions, like who is eligible to vote, away from the states."

Talwani’s June 25 permanent injunction barred USPS from completing portions of the rulemaking process for the 2026 election.

FEDERAL APPEALS COURT REJECTS TRUMP BID TO ENFORCE MAIL BALLOT ORDER AHEAD OF MIDTERM ELECTIONS

The dispute reached the Supreme Court, which stayed Talwani’s earlier judgment on Aug. 24 after concluding that the Trump administration was likely to prevail on its argument that the original challenge was premature because USPS had not yet issued a final rule.

The justices did not decide whether the executive order or the subsequent USPS rule was lawful. After USPS finalized the policy, the Democratic-led states amended their lawsuit to directly challenge the rule. Talwani then issued the latest temporary restraining order.

"Ironically, the judge created that problem because her original injunction prevented the U.S. Postal Service from developing the rules earlier, months earlier, which would have allowed the states more time to prepare to follow the rule if the Supreme Court were to allow the rule to proceed," Teufel said.

"When the judge points to expenses and practical difficulties, those are expenses and difficulties created in part by the court itself—not by the rule and not by the attempted implementation of the rule," he added.

Talwani disputed that characterization in her latest order, writing that "no such delay occurred" because USPS had proceeded with publishing a proposed rule, receiving comments and issuing its final policy despite the earlier injunction.

POSTAL SERVICE THRUST INTO MAIL-IN BALLOT FIGHT AS TRUMP ORDER GETS TIED UP IN COURT

Despite his criticism, Teufel stopped short of accusing Talwani of acting for partisan reasons.

"It’s hard for me to accuse the court of partisanship based on the information I have at the present time," Teufel said. "Certainly, the court exceeded its authority in issuing the initial injunction against the executive order, which is not a good look."

Talwani is set to hear arguments Thursday on the challengers’ request for a preliminary injunction, which could block the USPS rule for a longer period as the litigation continues. The existing 14-day temporary restraining order remains in place in the meantime while the Trump administration’s appeal of Talwani’s earlier judgment is pending before the First Circuit.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Snead argued that the legal dispute turns on whether USPS is regulating elections or merely setting conditions for the mail it carries.

"What the government counters is that this is just a Postal Service rule like any other and that the Postal Service has broad authority to regulate the mail that is using the Postal Service," Snead said. "This is essentially the same sort of rule as requiring that mail pieces be in envelopes, for instance, or have postage paid."

Even if the policy does not take effect for the midterms, Snead said states should have ample time to comply before the next presidential election.

"This is a very mundane rule, very simple to comply with, especially on the kind of timeline that we’re talking about in preparation for 2028," Snead said. "It’s not about being able to comply with this rule. It is just about resisting efforts to bring greater transparency and security to mail voting."

item.title: Kai Trump reveals emotional college transition, claims she 'hasn't eaten in like three days'
item.description: Kai Trump's vlog captures her emotional move to the University of Miami, from tearful goodbyes to strep throat derailing her first week on the golf team.
item.content:encoded:
Kai Trump, the 19-year-old granddaughter of President Donald Trump, detailed her emotional transition to college life in a video posted to her YouTube channel, capturing everything from early-morning team meetings to an unexpected bout of strep throat during her first week at the University of Miami.

The video documents her final days in Jupiter, Florida, before moving into her apartment to join the University of Miami women’s golf team as a freshman.

During the drive home after playing a round of golf before her move, Kai spoke about the stress of leaving her home routine behind.

KAI TRUMP RECALLS ‘A LOT OF CRYING’ WITH MOM VANESSA BEFORE COLLEGE AMID BREAST CANCER BATTLE

"I’ve been like literally sobbing," she said.

"It’s just like really sad that I have to say goodbye to like everyone today. I’m not like a very emotional person at all, so this is like really weird for me to cry."

She added, "I’m just struggling right now just like thinking about it, but like I’m excited."

Once Kai arrived in Miami, her best friend, Emma, helped her move in and brought along groceries to make sure she was eating during the busy move.

KAI TRUMP REVEALS HOW FAMILY RALLIED AROUND MOM VANESSA AMID BREAST CANCER BATTLE: ‘IT’S A LONG JOURNEY’

"Emma got me some frozen foods because I haven't eaten in like three days," Kai said in the video.

As classes began, the president’s granddaughter chronicled the early start to her athletic and academic responsibilities, noting a 7 a.m. team meeting on her first Monday.

"I’m very tired if you guys cannot tell by my face," she said while getting ready.

"I got sick with strep on Wednesday, my first week of school," Kai told viewers later in the vlog.

item.title: DHS condemns Rosie O’Donnell after ‘disgusting’ claim that detained immigrants are raped in ICE facilities
item.description: Rosie O'Donnell claimed ICE facilities are "concentration camps" where children are raped, prompting DHS to call her smears categorically false.
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Homeland Security condemned comedian Rosie O’Donnell and set the record straight after she made multiple wild claims about ICE facilities.

In a TikTok titled, "Friday Ramble," O'Donnell discussed a variety of topics, including the recent death of country music legend Dolly Parton, before launching into criticism of the Trump administration.

"We all vowed ‘Never Again,’ remember?" she said in the TikTok video, referencing the Holocaust. She noted that people even today are shocked at how Germans allowed fascism to take over before claiming fascism is in full swing in the United States.

WHITE HOUSE BRINGS RECEIPTS AFTER MEDIA CLAIMS NONCRIMINAL ICE ARRESTS ‘SOARING’: ‘FALSE NARRATIVES’

"We’re making concentration camps. … We’re rounding up people without a warrant. We’re raping children in detention, in ICE detention. They’re all getting pregnant," she said. 

"And they’re separated, males and females. Who has access to those girls? What happens to their babies? What do they do with them? There are big questions."

While some public figures, like Joe Concha and the White House, have already blasted O’Donnell for her comments, a spokesman for the DHS rejected her claims in comments to Fox News Digital.

"These disgusting, reckless and categorically FALSE smears are directly contributing to our officers facing a 1,300% increase in assaults, a 3,300% increase in vehicular attacks and an 8,000% increase in death threats against them," the spokesman for the DHS said in an exclusive statement. 

"Moreover, comparisons of illegal alien detention centers to internment camps used during World War II are deranged and lazy.

"These celebrities remain quiet about the humanitarian crisis that was manufactured by the Biden administration’s open border policies and the several hundred thousand children exploited, trafficked and missing on their watch," the spokesman added. 

"Under President Trump, ICE is dedicated to locating these unaccompanied children that came in through the border under Biden. Sadly, the extremely unstable, TDS-suffering lunatic Rosie O’Donnell — who fled the country in protest of President Trump’s historic, landslide re-election — would rather spin fake news that benefits the traffickers, smugglers and rapists than acknowledge the nightmare so many children lived under Democrat control.

"Our agents are focused on protecting the American people — not entertaining performative outrage. Where is the outrage for angel families who lost a loved one to illegal alien crime?" the spokesman asked. 

"To most Americans, our brave ICE law enforcement are heroes. Eighty percent of Americans support arresting and deporting criminal illegal aliens from American neighborhoods. These officers put their lives on the line every day to arrest the worst of the worst, including murderers, pedophiles, rapists, gang members and terrorists.

ANGEL DAD TAKES MAJOR NEW ROLE AFTER DAUGHTER’S KILLING SPARKS SWEEPING ILLEGAL ALIEN CRACKDOWN

"ICE has authority for lawful arrests where authorized under 8 USC 1357. Law enforcement officers use ‘reasonable suspicion’ to investigate immigration status and probable cause to make arrests consistent with the statute and the Fourth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution. The Supreme Court has already vindicated us on these practices," the spokesman added.

The department disputed O'Donnell's claims about conditions at ICE facilities.

"Claims that there are subprime conditions at ICE detention centers are FALSE. ICE has higher detention standards than most U.S. prisons that hold actual U.S. citizens," the DHS spokesman added in the statement. 

"All detainees are provided with three meals a day, clean water, clothing, bedding, showers, soap and toiletries. Illegal aliens also have access to phones to communicate with their family members and lawyers. Certified dieticians evaluate meals. In fact, ICE has higher detention standards than most U.S. prisons that hold actual U.S. citizens.

"It is a longstanding practice to provide comprehensive medical care from the moment an alien enters ICE custody. This includes medical, dental and mental health services as available and access to medical appointments and 24-hour emergency care. For many illegal aliens, this is the best healthcare they have received their entire lives," he added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The department also pushed back against the actress's claims about pregnant detainees.

"Pregnancy in ICE detention is exceedingly rare, making up 0.15% of all illegal aliens currently in custody, as of June 30," the DHS spokesman said. 

"Pregnant women receive regular prenatal visits, mental health services, nutritional support and accommodations aligned with community standards of care. In addition to medical, mental health and dental services provided to all detained women as required by ICE detention standards, facilities provide women with pregnancy services such as pregnancy testing, routine or specialized prenatal care, postpartum follow-up and nursing services."

O'Donnell has a long history of blasting the Trump administration, particularly ICE enforcement.

In July 2025, she made similar comparisons between ICE and Nazi Germany, saying, "I think Americans should stand up and say, ‘No way. You’re not going to silence us. You don’t have the right to silence us. You never did. And you never will. We, the people, have the right to speak up against atrocities which are happening on a daily basis.’ ICE, his own personal Gestapo — what will it take, America? What will it take?

"He’s going to arrest every artist that disagrees with him, and pretty much every artist does," she said. "Whether or not they’re brave enough to say it is another thing."

"Being in detention is a choice," the DHS spokesman said. "We encourage all illegal aliens to take control of their departure with the CBP Home App. The United States is offering illegal aliens $3,000 and a free flight to self-deport now. We encourage every person here illegally to take advantage of this offer and reserve the chance to come back to the U.S. the right legal way to live the American dream. If not, you will be arrested and deported without a chance to return."

"Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin, ICE is targeting the worst of the worst," the spokesman concluded. "Nearly 70% of ICE arrests are of illegal aliens charged or convicted of a crime in the U.S. Our message is clear: If you come into our country illegally and break our laws, we will find you wherever you are, we will arrest you and we will deport you."

Fox News Digital reached out to Rosie O’Donnell’s management and did not receive an immediate reply.

item.title: Amazon drone delivery is coming to nearly 500 cities
item.description: Amazon Prime Air drone delivery plans to reach nearly 500 U.S. cities by the end of 2026, but your yard and ZIP code may determine eligibility.
item.content:encoded:
Amazon wants to make waiting for a package feel almost old-fashioned. Its Prime Air drone delivery service is gearing up for a major expansion, with plans to reach nearly 500 U.S. cities and towns by the end of 2026. For some shoppers, that could mean getting an eligible Amazon order dropped at home in as fast as 30 minutes.

That is a huge jump from where things stand today. Amazon currently operates Prime Air from 11 U.S. locations across 10 metro areas, and the company says its drones have already delivered hundreds of thousands of packages this year.

There is one detail worth keeping in mind when you hear that 500-city figure. Amazon is talking about communities served, rather than 500 individual drone hubs. Each Prime Air site can cover about 175 square miles, allowing one launch location to reach several nearby cities and towns.

So, could one of these drones soon be heading toward your neighborhood? Here's where Prime Air is available now, what it costs and what you should know before choosing drone delivery at checkout.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats , has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com

DRONE DELIVERS 2 PIZZAS IN MINUTES

Prime Air currently serves the Phoenix, Tampa, Kansas City, Baton Rouge, Detroit, Omaha, Houston, Dallas, San Antonio and Waco metro areas. Those markets span seven states. Amazon says Chicago, Syracuse, Cleveland, Atlanta and Boise are next on its launch list. More communities are expected later this year.

If you live in one of those metro areas, that still does not guarantee a drone will appear as a delivery choice. Amazon says coverage can vary by ZIP code and address. When your home qualifies, the drone option appears while you shop or at checkout. That is the easiest way to know whether Prime Air has reached you. You do not need a separate app or a special Amazon account.

Amazon advertises Prime Air delivery in as fast as 30 minutes. However, the company says most drone orders currently arrive around 60 minutes after checkout. That could still save you a trip when you need something quickly. If you need a charger before a trip or medicine you would rather not drive out for, an hour can feel very different from waiting until tomorrow.

Amazon says Prime Air can carry packages up to 5 pounds that fit roughly inside a large shoebox. The company says that makes more than 60% of the items customers buy most often eligible for drone delivery. The selection can include iPhones, Galaxy phones, AirPods, AirTags, Ring doorbells, groceries and household products. Of course, the exact selection depends on your location and what Amazon can safely load onto the drone.

UFC STAR CONOR MCGREGOR GOES VIRAL FOR DRONE DELIVERY FIASCO AFTER UNDERGOING KNEE SURGERY

What you pay for drone delivery depends on whether you have Prime and how much you order. Prime members pay no drone delivery fee when an eligible order totals $50 or more. Prime members pay $2.99 on smaller eligible orders. Customers without Prime pay $4.99.

That pricing could make drone delivery tempting when you need something quickly. On the other hand, paying a fee to shave a few hours off a routine purchase may feel unnecessary. The bigger question may be how quickly you begin treating one-hour delivery as normal once it becomes available.

If Prime Air is available at your address, you will see the drone delivery option when you check out on Amazon. For your first order, you choose a delivery spot on your property. You can use that same spot again or change it later. When the drone arrives, it checks the area before releasing your package. Amazon says it looks for people, pets, vehicles and other obstacles that could get in the way.

That also means your yard could determine whether drone delivery works for you. Trees, landscaping or a pool may make it harder for the drone to find a safe place to drop your order. As Prime Air expands into more neighborhoods, Amazon will have to make sure each delivery spot gives the drone enough room to do its job safely.

Amazon holds FAA Part 135 certification for Prime Air, the federal framework used for commercial drone package delivery. The FAA says Part 135 certification provides the path for operators carrying someone else's property for compensation beyond visual line of sight. Prime Air also uses a Detect-and-Avoid system. Amazon says the drone continuously scans the airspace around it and makes real-time decisions to avoid obstacles while flying.

Then there is the privacy question. Prime Air drones use onboard cameras and sensors for navigation. Amazon says the drones do not track individuals or record their movements. The company also says no person watches a live camera feed, because the drone processes the camera data onboard for navigation.

Noise may be the more noticeable issue for many neighborhoods. Amazon says the drone produces less sound during drop-off than an idling delivery truck parked at the curb. At cruising altitude, the company compares the sound with a window fan on low. Still, community complaints about drone noise have followed delivery programs before. As Amazon expands, local reaction could shape how smoothly Prime Air enters some neighborhoods.

Amazon first showed off the idea of 30-minute drone delivery more than a decade ago. Since then, engineers have redesigned the aircraft while Amazon worked through aviation rules and local concerns. Now the company believes it has a version that can scale. Amazon CEO Andy Jassy told shareholders this year that Prime Air expects to reach communities with about 30 million customers by year-end. He also said the company plans to deliver half a billion packages by the end of the decade. Even with that ambition, drones will handle only a small slice of Amazon's overall deliveries for now. A drone carries one lightweight package at a time, while vans and trucks can move much larger loads.

Amazon also has plenty of competition. Walmart and Alphabet-owned Wing plan to expand drone delivery to more than 270 Walmart stores by 2027. Meanwhile, DoorDash has received FAA Part 135 certification for its own drone operation. The race has moved beyond proving that a drone can carry a package. Companies now have to show that people will use the service regularly and that neighborhoods will accept more aircraft overhead.

For most people, the first sign that Prime Air has reached their area will be simple: a drone delivery option shows up at checkout. If you need something quickly, that could be genuinely useful. A forgotten charger, medicine or another small item could arrive before you would normally make it to the store and back.

There are some limits to keep in mind. Your order has to fit Amazon's size and weight rules, your property needs a safe drop spot and bad weather can delay a flight. You may also have to decide how much speed is worth to you. More drone deliveries could mean more noise overhead and more questions about how these aircraft fit into everyday neighborhoods. If Prime Air becomes available at your address, I would try it when you actually need something fast. That is probably the best way to find out whether 30-minute delivery feels genuinely useful in your day-to-day life.

FIREWORKS ARE FADING, BUT THEIR HIGH-TECH REPLACEMENT COMES WITH NEW RISKS

Amazon has been chasing 30-minute drone delivery since Jeff Bezos introduced the idea in 2013. For years, it felt like a technology that was always coming soon. The scale of this new plan changes that conversation. I do not expect delivery vans to disappear. A 5-pound payload, changing weather, tricky yards and local rules give ground delivery plenty of work to do. But when you need a small item quickly, getting it in 30 to 60 minutes could become genuinely useful. What catches my attention most is how fast expectations can change. Same-day delivery once sounded incredibly fast. Now Amazon wants you thinking about whether an hour feels too long.

Would you welcome Amazon drones over your neighborhood if they could get an order to your home in under an hour, or would you rather keep those deliveries on the road? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

item.title: Taylor Swift's husband Travis Kelce reveals what really happened at their 'insane' wedding
item.description: The Kelce brothers spill behind-the-scenes details from the Taylor Swift wedding at Madison Square Garden, from the guest list to the last call.
item.content:encoded:
Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift’s star-studded wedding was such a party that Jason Kelce joked guests had to be "kicked out" of Madison Square Garden when the night finally came to an end.

More than a month after Travis and Swift tied the knot, the Kelce brothers detailed the over-the-top celebration on their "New Heights" podcast, spilling behind-the-scenes details about the couple’s ultra-private big day for the first time publicly.

"They kicked us out," Jason quipped after Travis admitted the night went by in the "blink of an eye."

TRAVIS KELCE CALLS MARRYING TAYLOR SWIFT AT MADISON SQUARE GARDEN 'THE BEST NIGHT OF MY LIFE'

Travis quickly revealed what really happened, explaining that guests began filtering out once the drinks stopped flowing.

"Well, they stopped – once the drinks stopped being served, everyone kind of just starts to, you know, mosey out," Travis said.

item.title: Caitlin Clark shows the WNBA how to respect America, Belichick's tricks & NFL host Colleen Wolfe loves summer!
item.description: Caitlin Clark shared how grateful she is to represent Team USA at the FIBA Women's World Cup in Berlin, setting a tone few WNBA athletes match.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

First Hump Day of September. I'd say this is our biggest Hump Day of the year so far.

We've got college football for the next five days, starting tomorrow night. That's right. We have Week 1 games tomorrow night. It's here. We've done it.

SEC LAWYERS, LANE KIFFIN AND DEATH VALLEY: COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S WEEK 1 IS SET FOR FIREWORKS

I begged everyone to get the chores done the past five weeks, because this day was coming. I hope everyone got that yard in order, because free weekends are officially OVER.

How about this for a sign: I mowed yesterday after being gone all weekend in Daytona. Yard was a MESS. Right at the end, my mower gave out. She just stopped. I tried cranking her back up, and it immediately smelled like it was overheating.

Her watch has now ended. Football season has begun. Rest easy.

Welcome to a Hump Day Nightcaps — the one where Caitlin Clark shows proper respect to this great country.

Patriot.

What else? I've got NFL reporter Colleen Wolfe ending summer on a high note before the season starts (in one week!), a new conspiracy involving Bill Belichick and the Patriots, and the influencers are wreaking HAVOC at the U.S. Open.

CAITLIN CLARK AND ANGEL REESE MUST NOW WORK TOGETHER AT WOMEN'S WORLD CUP AS WNBA TAKES A HIGH-STAKES BREAK

Is this the most infuriating video of the day? The week? Has to be up there, right? You'll see.

OK, grab you something patriotic and settle in for a first-Hump-Day-of-September 'Cap!

Yes, I know it's football season. I know the WNBA is off for a few weeks. I get it. There should be other things to talk about today, but, to be honest, it's slow out there.

It's the week before a holiday weekend, after all. The news cycle tends to slow down just a bit this week before ramping up for good until we ring in the new year.

So, yes — we're gonna go back to the well and start with Caitlin Clark.

For those who don't know, she's playing in Berlin this month with the rest of Team USA in the FIBA Women's World Cup. It's her first time on the team after being passed over two years ago.

Remember how dumb that was? Amazing.

BUT, Caitlin got the nod this year, and she made it clear today that she plans to honor this great country.

That ain't always a guarantee with the WNBA folks, you know? Don't know if you've heard, but they can be a bit ... volatile ... when it comes to the US of A.

Not Clark:

"It's crazy, and I think you know, you get used to it," she told FIBA's official website before Friday's opening tip against China. "I think at the same time, I almost think about it another way. Like, how lucky am I? This is pretty special and pretty cool, and there's so many people that would kill to be in this spot and have this type of opportunity."

"Especially to play for the USA team, let alone play in the WNBA and live out your dream every single day. So I try to look at, look at it the other way and think about how lucky I am and how grateful I am."

Yep. She gets it. Isn't it amazing how low the bar is right now when it comes to patting athletes on the back? Especially WNBA athletes?

Caitlin Clark simply said, "How lucky am I?" when talking about playing for the USA, and it went mega-viral on the internet. That's all it takes. It's all we ask at this point.

There does seem to have been a shift in American pride since the women's soccer team embarrassed us a few years back. You saw it earlier this year with the men's and women's hockey teams in the Olympics.

And then with the baseball team in the World Baseball Classic.

Obviously, we saw it all summer with the men's soccer team.

This will be a huge test, though — both for the players and the fans back here in America. How do they represent us? And, how do we respond? The WNBA is a lightning rod right now.

This was a good first test, and Caitlin Clark passed. Well done!

OK, let's keep this class flowing and gear up for some NFL football with the wildest conspiracy theory on the internet today, courtesy of former NFL analytics man, Ryan Paganetti:

"I went through more than a decade of TV broadcasts and uncovered a diabolically clever piece of Patriots gamesmanship," Paganetti said in a now-viral social media post.

"When opposing kickers lined up at Gillette Stadium, the video board displayed a reverse view of the kick, placing a second, offset set of yellow uprights directly behind the real ones.

"I found dozens of examples. In the same games, I reviewed 52 Patriots field goal attempts. The illusion appeared on Patriots kicks exactly zero times."

Whoaaaaaaa Nellie! No idea if this was intentional or not, but given the history of the 2001-2019 Patriots ... it's certainly in the playbook.

Putting the goal posts on the scoreboard, directly behind the actual goal posts, to try and confuse opposing kickers is so perfectly Bill Belichick, it hurts. No stone left unturned!

And for those who want to see it in action ...

I remember watching Billy Cundiff miss that field goal and just being numb for hours. I was sitting in the dining hall my first year at college, watching with a bunch of Pats fans, and I couldn't believe it. Even as a long-suffering Dolphins fan, that one hurt.

Makes more sense now!

OK, let's rapid-fire this Hump Day class into a big Hump Day night. First up? The insufferable TikTok influencers are at it AGAIN:

Good Lord. Look at them. Just listen to that nonsense. Intolerable.

Danny continued on in a separate tweet:

"It was at 11:44pm on Monday right in the middle of the Osaka match," he said. "The chair umpire turned around and told the specific suite to be quiet."

We used to be such a proper country. We had it so good, and we just pissed it all away. What a fall from grace.

Sad.

OK, that's it for today. Let's not end Hump Day on a sour note, though. NFL starts in ONE WEEK.

NFL Network host Colleen Wolfe is excited, and we are, too!

See you tomorrow.

Will the rest of the WNBA athletes follow Caitlin's lead? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

item.title: Spanberger's ICE restrictions dealt major setback as judge warns other blue states
item.description: A federal judge blocked a key part of Gov. Abigail Spanberger's law restricting local 287(g) cooperation with ICE, and Republicans say they warned her.
item.content:encoded:
A judge paused a key part of Virginia’s new restrictions on local cooperation with federal immigration authorities, handing Gov. Abigail Spanberger’s administration a major legal setback as a similar fight plays out in neighboring Maryland.

George H.W. Bush-appointed Judge Robert Payne on Monday blocked a key piece of a law signed by Gov. Abigail Spanberger that heavily restricts interagency cooperation and would have required local sheriffs to modify or dissolve their individual policies, known as 287(g) agreements, by a Tuesday deadline.

Payne ruled the federal government is likely to prevail on several claims in its lawsuit against Virginia, finding "the Virginia 287(g) Law violates the Contracts Clause [of the] U.S. Constitution because it is a ‘substantial impairment’ of the existing contracts between the federal government and Virginia localities."

Payne did not strike down the law but paused its implementation as the feds’ case against Richmond proceeds.

FIRST ON FOX: DOJ SUES SPANBERGER’S VIRGINIA OVER LAWS KNEECAPPING FEDERAL AGENTS AS MASK WAR ESCALATES

He also found that Virginia’s law wrongly attempts to "regulate conduct of federal law enforcement in the enforcement of federal immigration laws."

"At this point, saying ‘I told you so’ seems almost pointless," Virginia House Minority Leader Terry Kilgore, R-Gate City, told Fox News Digital when responding to the news.

LEGAL EXPERT UNLEASHES ON SPANBERGER'S NEW EXECUTIVE ORDER TARGETING ICE: 'POLITICAL THEATER'

Kilgore said Republicans repeatedly warned Spanberger’s administration that its limits on cooperation with ICE would waste taxpayer money and run into these kinds of legal problems.

"States cannot tell the federal government how to do its job. But Democrats refused to listen," Kilgore said.

In that regard, Rep. Ben Cline, R-Va., drafted a bill at the federal level aimed directly at Spanberger’s law.

Cline’s 287(g) Cooperation Act would require state and local law enforcement to enter into interagency agreements with ICE as a condition of receiving federal Community-Oriented Policing (COPS) grants.

Additionally, all five of Virginia’s Republican members of Congress wrote Spanberger earlier this year urging her not to undo former Gov. Glenn Youngkin’s statewide directive of Richmond-Washington cooperation on the immigration enforcement front.

The major setback to Democrats’ plans came as neighboring Maryland found itself in a similar legal fight, though a judge has not yet ruled in that case.

HOCHUL REMAINS DEFIANT AFTER SHERIFFS SUE OVER LAW BANNING COOPERATION WITH ICE: 'BRING IT ON'

Gov. Wes Moore allowed a similar bill to become law earlier this year that would prevent most cooperation between local sheriffs and ICE. Despite Maryland being one of the bluest states in the union, the majority of its counties are geographically red.

That dynamic revealed itself as 17 of its 24 sheriffs, led by Harford County’s Jeffrey Gahler, Wicomico County’s Mike Lewis and Frederick County’s Charles Jenkins launched a lawsuit against the law.

"They want to do everything they can to handcuff law enforcement, handcuff sheriffs across the state," Jenkins said in March.

Sen. Clarence Lam, D-Elkridge, a bill sponsor, argued the measure ensures local jails won’t be used as a "front door to the federal government’s oftentimes deportation pipeline," according to Maryland Matters.

Lam’s Community Trust Act requires a court order to provide immigration-related information and to transfer inmates based on immigration status, according to the outlet.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Moore did not sign the legislation, but it became law after he notified Senate President Bill Ferguson IV, D-Baltimore, of his decision after the bill passed 32-15.

Gahler’s coalition later sued, setting up a potentially similar battle in Greenbelt federal court to the one making a splash across the Potomac.

item.title: What is a Tuey-Rodriguez charge? Judge gives instruction to deadlocked Lindsay Clancy jury
item.description: The judge in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial issued a rare Tuey-Rodriguez charge after jurors again said they were deadlocked. Learn what the Massachusetts jury instruction is.
item.content:encoded:
A Massachusetts judge overseeing the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy gave jurors a Tuey-Rodriguez charge Wednesday after they reported for a second time that they were unable to reach a unanimous verdict.

The instruction is given to a deadlocked jury to encourage continued deliberations while reminding jurors they should not abandon honestly held beliefs simply to reach a verdict.

Judge William Sullivan sent jurors back to deliberate Tuesday after they first indicated they were struggling to agree. After the jury again reported that it was deadlocked, Sullivan delivered the formal charge.

A Tuey-Rodriguez charge is unique to Massachusetts and is sometimes called a "dynamite charge" because it is intended to help break a jury impasse without coercing a verdict.

LINDSAY CLANCY VERDICT STILL WITHIN REACH – RETIRED MASSACHUSETTS JUDGE PUSHES BACK ON HUNG-JURY PREDICTIONS

The instruction takes its name from two Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court decisions. In Commonwealth v. Tuey (1851), the court approved an instruction encouraging deadlocked jurors to re-examine their views with an open mind. More than a century later, in Commonwealth v. Rodriguez (1973), the state's highest court revised that language to remove pressure on minority or holdout jurors, creating a neutral instruction that asks all jurors to carefully consider one another's views while maintaining their own honestly held convictions.

Receiving a Tuey-Rodriguez charge does not mean a verdict is imminent. The instruction is generally considered a necessary step before a judge declares a mistrial because of a hung jury, although it often results in jurors reaching a unanimous verdict after further deliberations.

LINDSAY CLANCY’S FUTURE COULD REST WITH ‘PROSECUTION DOCTORS’ AS CASE ECHOES INFAMOUS MAINE KILLINGS: EXPERT

Retired Massachusetts Superior Court Judge Thomas Drechsler told Fox News Digital the instruction is typically given only after a judge determines jurors have fully deliberated but remain deadlocked.

"The charge encourages the jurors to rethink their own feelings in light of what other jurors feel" while reminding them that no one is in a better position to decide the case than the jurors who heard all the evidence, Drechsler said.

If jurors report they remain deadlocked after receiving the instruction, "there's a higher likelihood" the case could end in a mistrial, Drechsler said, though he noted he has seen juries return verdicts after receiving a Tuey-Rodriguez charge.

Clancy faces three counts of first-degree murder in the January 2023 deaths of her three children — Cora, Dawson and Callan — at the family's Duxbury, Massachusetts, home.

She does not dispute killing the children but argues she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and was not criminally responsible at the time. Prosecutors contend Clancy was legally sane and intentionally planned the killings.

Jurors will continue deliberating after receiving the Tuey-Rodriguez charge. If they remain unable to reach a unanimous verdict, Sullivan could declare a mistrial, leaving prosecutors to decide whether to seek a new trial.

item.content:encoded:
Women who start hormone replacement therapy (HRT) at a certain age may have a lower dementia risk, a new study suggests.

The study, published in Alzheimer’s & Dementia, analyzed UK Biobank data of 183,450 postmenopausal women averaging 60 years of age.

The U.K. researchers determined that HRT use was associated with about a 10% lower risk of all-cause dementia and a 16% lower risk of Alzheimer’s disease over a 13-year follow-up period.

'LONGEVITY GENE' MAY PROTECT THE BRAIN FROM ALZHEIMER'S BY BOOSTING DNA REPAIR, STUDY FINDS

The association was strongest among women who started the therapy between the ages of 46 and 56. It was also high among those who had undergone surgical menopause.

Starting HRT after age 56 was not associated with reduced dementia risk.

Dr. Alexa Fiffick, a board-certified family medicine physician and founder of Concierge Medicine of Westlake in Cleveland, Ohio, noted that this was an observational study that can’t show cause and effect.

"So, it kind of stays where the data has been for a while — that in certain patients, we have no evidence that it really makes a difference," she told Fox News Digital.

7 NEW DEMENTIA RISK FACTORS REVEALED — INCLUDING ONE MILLIONS STRUGGLE WITH

"And, for some patients, such as [those] who go through menopause a little bit younger, whether that's surgically or naturally, or if they have that APOE ε4 genotype that predisposes them to dementia, there may be some benefit."

The researchers also stated that since this was an observational study, it could not establish that HRT prevents dementia but only showed an association.

The study also did not assess any safety outcomes or adverse events related to HRT.

Women who use HRT may differ from non-users in other ways that affect dementia risk, such as their overall health, lifestyle or access to healthcare, the researchers noted.

Although researchers adjusted for many of these factors, some unmeasured differences could still factor into the lower dementia risk seen among HRT users.

The study also did not have detailed information on the types of hormone therapy, the way they were administered or the specific dosages women took.

Most of the people in the study were of European ancestry and tended to be better off financially, so the findings may not apply equally to people from other populations.

This study alone likely doesn't warrant seeking out HRT just for dementia prevention, Fiffick said.

"However, if you're having symptoms, if you feel not yourself, come in, talk to your doctor, have that conversation," she advised.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

There is some data linking menopausal symptoms, such as hot flashes and night sweats, with vascular changes in the brain, the doctor noted.

"So, we are very hopeful to see that treating those symptoms may prevent the vascular changes that lead to vascular dementia, but we just don't have that data right now," she said. 

"So, it's worth the conversation, it's worth bringing up, but I wouldn't go out of your way for just this purpose."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

HRT does carry some known risks and side effects, Fiffick noted.

For oral versions of estrogen, there may be an increased risk of blood clots. That risk does not appear to exist for transdermal options, such as patches, gels and creams.

Other types of HRT may impact breast activity, overall inflammation, cardiovascular markers and cardiometabolic markers, according to the doctor.

"So, it's not one size fits all, and it's really worth an extensive conversation."

The U.K. researchers plan to conduct randomized controlled trials to confirm that HRT reduces dementia risk. Future studies will include factors such as estrogen-only versus combined therapy, dosage amounts, administration route, treatment duration, age at the start of therapy, menopause type and potentially APOE genotype.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"I think the more we have studies like this, the more we're going to propel forward the randomized controlled trials to really give women the data they deserve," Fiffick concluded.

"Women deserve to have information to use to make decisions about their bodies. So I'm excited to see the trends heading in that direction."

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed dubbed ‘veteran’ by Soros-linked propaganda newspaper distributed in Michigan
item.description: A Soros-funded propaganda newspaper falsely labeled Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed a veteran in a headline distributed statewide.
item.content:encoded:

"El-Sayed — veteran, doctor, and former health official — is Democratic Senate pick," reads a headline in the August 2026 edition of The Michigan Independent.

LIZ PEEK: MICHIGAN CAN STOP THE SOCIALIST FEVER RAGE — OR WATCH IT SWALLOW THE SENATE

TOP MEDIA OUTLETS FAIL TO DISCLOSE WHO IS BANKROLLING THEIR AI REPORTERS

In 2024, The American Independent Foundation, a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization, received a $500,000 grant from George Soros' Foundation to Promote Open Society, according to that organization's IRS 990 disclosure form.

Some of the outlets share the same featured stories. At the time of this writing, both The Ohio Independent and The Pennsylvania Independent feature a story titled "Report: Trump and Big Oil see financial windfall as Americans pay more at pump".

SOROS NETWORK REBUILDS PROGRESSIVE PROSECUTOR PUSH AFTER STRING OF ELECTION LOSSES

An associated 501(c)(4) political activism organization, American Independent Media, is also affiliated with the network of news outlets. Each state-based website says it is a project of American Independent Media whose mission is "to use journalism to educate the public, giving them the information they need about local and federal issues."

David Brock, founder of the far-left media watchdog Media Matters and a high-profile Democratic operative, is also connected to the shadowy network of papers.

DEM SENATE HOPEFUL’S ‘PHYSICIAN’ CAMPAIGN PITCH UNDER FIRE AFTER LICENSE RECORDS REVEAL KEY GAPS

item.title: Where Tunnel to Towers' Steel Across America tour will stop ahead of 9/11
item.description: A 21-foot steel beam from the South Tower of the World Trade Center heads to Fenway Park, D.C., and MetLife Stadium for the 9/11 anniversary.
item.content:encoded:
A 21-foot steel beam recovered from the South Tower of the World Trade Center will make its way up the East Coast this week as part of the Tunnel to Towers Foundation’s Steel Across America tour.

The tour kicked off earlier this year as a way to mark the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks and celebrate American service members and first responders. The steel will stop in Massachusetts, Washington, D.C., and New York City through Sept. 11.

Wednesday night's stop will be at the Boston Red Sox vs. Seattle Mariners game at Fenway Park in Boston, before heading to the Massachusetts Fallen Heroes Memorial on Thursday.

AMERICA’S HEARTLAND COMES FACE-TO-FACE WITH 9/11 HISTORY AS 25TH ANNIVERSARY NEARS

The 16,900-pound beam will then head to the nation's capital, where it will be featured at a private event on Friday. It will then head to New York City for another private event in Brooklyn on Sept. 11, before a final appearance at the New York Giants vs. Dallas Cowboys game at MetLife Stadium on Sept. 13.

The beam visited the U.S. Military Academy at West Point on Monday, where the superintendent, Lt. Gen. James B. Bartholomees III, said the piece of steel connects the courage shown by first responders on 9/11 with the Americans who answered the call to serve in the years that followed.

MASSIVE PIECE OF 9/11 HISTORY MAKES STUNNING 10,500-MILE JOURNEY ACROSS AMERICA

"As we approach the 25th anniversary of 9/11, this piece of steel reminds us of the courage of first responders like Stephen Siller and the countless Americans who answered the call in the years that followed, including generations of West Point graduates," Bartholomees said. "Today, young men and women continue that legacy of service, guided by duty, honor country."

The ceremony brought together cadets, faculty, staff and guests and opened with a color guard and pipe and drum procession by members of the NYPD, FDNY and Port Authority Police Department. The program also included the national anthem, an invocation and blessing of the steel, and a moment of reflection accompanied by "Amazing Grace."

BENJAMIN HALL TACKLES GRUELING ONE WORLD TRADE CENTER CLIMB ON PROSTHETIC LEGS TO HONOR FALLEN HEROES

Frank Siller, chairman and CEO of Tunnel to Towers and the brother of fallen FDNY firefighter Stephen Siller, recalled his brother’s final actions on Sept. 11.

"Twenty-five years ago, my brother Stephen strapped on 60 pounds of gear and ran through the Brooklyn Battery Tunnel toward danger, duty and the people who needed him inside those towers," Siller said.

"Duty, honor, country: Those values connect West Point cadets, Stephen and first responders all across this country," he continued. "We are grateful to West Point for welcoming us, and we leave more committed than ever to making sure the sacrifice of Sept. 11 is never forgotten."

item.description: President Donald Trump said Tiger Woods suffers "great pain" from back issues and urged him to get a driver, reacting to the golfer's reckless driving plea deal.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump reacted to Tiger Woods’ plea agreement on Wednesday.

Trump, who is close with the legendary golfer, lamented Woods suffering "great pain" as he’s dealt with persistent back issues for several years.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"Look, I know Tiger, very well. He's a great guy," the president told Fox News Channel's Peter Doocy. "He's unique in so many ways, especially as an athlete, but also as a man. He suffers great pain, great pain. It's a very tough situation because they didn't find alcohol on him. He didn't test positive at all for alcohol. But because of his horrible back – he had, my opinion, a bad doctor – but he had a back operation that did not work out well. And he is under pain.

"And so, it's a tough deal when you're taking a painkiller because you're under pain and tremendous pain and you have a problem and you test positive. He would have told him that. Why don't you get somebody to drive you? So, he's going to have somebody drive him from now on. He's just a very special guy. I'm glad. I'm glad that was resolved."

Woods struck a plea deal ahead of his appearance in court. He pleaded no contest to the charges of willful, wanton reckless driving – second offense and a careless driving citation.

His license was suspended for five years.

The move came five months after the legendary golfer was involved in a rollover crash that led to charges of driving under the influence and refusal to submit to testing. He pleaded not guilty to the charges at first.

In March, Woods was traveling at a high rate of speed on Jupiter Island when his Land Rover clipped a truck and rolled onto its side. He managed to crawl out of the vehicle without any injuries. Woods agreed to a Breathalyzer, which showed no signs of alcohol. However, authorities said he refused a urine test. A sheriff’s office report said deputies discovered two pain pills in his pocket and showed signs of impairment.

Woods famously told responding officers he was on the phone with the president.

Woods later made his first public appearance since returning from the treatment in June. He helped introduce the PGA Tour’s plans to revamp its schedule for the 2028 season.

item.title: NFL's conduct policy review of Puka Nacua continues and that drives fantasy football managers nuts
item.description: Puka Nacua remains under NFL Personal Conduct Policy review amid a civil lawsuit, and discipline could still come even after the Rams' Week 1 opener.
item.content:encoded:
Puka Nacua may have NFL wide receiver superpowers, but that doesn't make him invisible to the league's ongoing Personal Conduct Policy review.

So the fact he was not suspended over the weekend when the league handed down discipline for three players – placing them on the Commissioner's Exempt List – does not mean Nacua has dodged discipline under the conduct policy.

Nacua, perhaps the Los Angeles Rams' most consistent offensive playmaker, is among a group of NFL employees whose situation is still under review after they got into some legal hot water in the offseason.

3 NFL STARS HIT COMMISSIONER'S EXEMPT LIST AFTER OFFSEASON FILLED WITH LEGAL TROUBLE

That list includes San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York, Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman, Rams offensive tackle Alaric Jackson and Nacua.

All, including Nacua, have off-field issues that have caused the NFL to review their individual situations, with a conduct policy rebuke still possible.

And this: The NFL's Week 1 games approaching is not a sign the men in focus will be in the clear once the regular season begins.

NFL FACING A DOMESTIC VIOLENCE EPIDEMIC THIS OFFSEASON WITH ARREST OF RAMS LINEMAN THE LATEST CASE

The NFL could suspend any of the players or York even after Week 1 if its independent investigations eventually determine that discipline is warranted. There is no firm league deadline requiring a Personal Conduct Policy decision before the season opener.

In 2024, for example, then-Buffalo Bills edge rusher Von Miller was suspended on Oct. 1 by the NFL after he had already played multiple games.

York is facing league scrutiny tied to his arrest on charges related to a prostitution sting last month.

Bateman and Jackson were both arrested on charges related to separate June incidents in separate incidents involving allegations of battery.

And Nacua, well, he's the defendant in a civil lawsuit filed by Madison Atiabi, who alleges he bit her shoulder during a New Year's Eve 2025 party.

RAMS TROUBLEMAKER WR PUKA NACUA SAYS HE'S A CHANGED MAN AFTER BITING INCIDENT AND STINT IN REHAB

Nacua’s attorney denies the allegations and characterizes the biting as "horseplay."

(Strange game, if true).

Anyway, a Los Angeles County judge has set a civil trial for March 27, 2028. No criminal charges have been filed.

The NFL has said nothing publicly beyond the fact that Nacua’s situation remains under league review. Nacua is currently expected to be available for Week 1 but that can change at any time.

And why is Nacua a focus here? Well, unlike any of the other players or York, Nacua is a major source of attention in fantasy football because of his prowess in real football.

So, countless fantasy football fans have been monitoring his status for their own selfish fantasy football reasons.

The Los Angeles Rams open their season in Australia on Sept. 10 against the San Francisco 49ers – with or without Nacua.

item.title: Nicolas Cage leads all-star cast in 'Fortitude,' a WWII film about the D-Day deception campaign

item.content:encoded:
The first preview is out for the upcoming World War II film "Fortitude" with Nicolas Cage.

Basic info:

WORLD WAR II VETERAN REVEALS 1-WORD FEELING BEFORE D-DAY 82 YEARS LATER

As the loyal readers know, I am obsessed with WWII history. I even spent part of my honeymoon touring WWII sites in France, including heavily in the Normandy region.

LAST SURVIVING 'ROSIE THE RIVETERS' HONORED BY WWII MUSEUM ON D-DAY ANNIVERSARY: 'WE CAN DO IT'

I'm always going to be interested in any WWII movie that's coming out. It's not a tough sell.

That leads me to "Fortitude" with Cage and Ben Kingsley. The first preview for the WWII film about Operation Fortitude was released Wednesday, and it looks like it's going to be electric.

Give the preview a watch below, and let me know your thoughts at David.Hookstead@outkick.com.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK CULTURE COVERAGE

For those who might not know, the Allies launched a massive deception campaign before D-Day aimed at convincing the Germans that the invasion of Western Europe would come through somewhere other than Normandy.

Specifically, the Allies wanted the Germans to believe the main landing would be at Pas-de-Calais. In order to achieve this goal, the Allies employed several deception tactics, including making fake vehicles and phantom armies that didn't exist.

In hindsight, it was one of the most brilliant moves in military history, and it helped give the brave men on the beaches in Normandy a better chance against the German forces tasked with holding the territory.

Now, the story will come to life with Nicolas Cage leading the way in "Fortitude."

item.title: Oakland coffee shop accused of kicking out Jewish dad, 5-year-old son and shutters amid antisemitism lawsuits
item.description: Jerusalem Coffee House faces a federal civil rights trial after the Justice Department alleged the Oakland cafe refused service to Jewish customers.
item.content:encoded:
Jerusalem Coffee House in Oakland, California, remained closed Wednesday after temporarily shutting its doors last week to focus on three lawsuits alleging it discriminated against Jewish customers, including a father and his 5-year-old son. The Palestinian-owned café is preparing for an October federal civil rights trial.

The coffeehouse announced in August that it would stop operating after Aug. 23 while its owners prepared for the litigation, including a Justice Department case scheduled for trial Oct. 26. 

A federal judge previously rejected the defendants’ attempt to dismiss the DOJ lawsuit, which alleges Fathi Abdulrahim Harara and employees refused service to Jewish customers wearing Star of David caps and followed them outside while hurling insults and threats.

The café blamed its legal problems on efforts to suppress its pro-Palestinian politics in an August statement on Substack, announcing the closure.

DOJ INVESTIGATING NYC COFFEE SHOP OVER HOSTILE SOCIAL POST ABOUT PRO-ISRAEL POLITICIAN

"These lawsuits represent the ongoing efforts of Zionist organizations and the federal government to use the courts as a tool to repress free speech and public political commitments to Palestine," it said.

Elizabeth Barcohana, the California Republican Party Jewish engagement chair and an attorney, criticized the shop’s defense of its conduct in a statement to Fox News Digital Wednesday.

"It is ironic that after freely expressing support for terrorism with these beverage names, the café owners appear to now be using the First Amendment as a defense for ejecting two Jewish customers who wore hats with Stars of David on them, in one case calling it a 'violent' hat," she said. 

"By their own standard, if a hat can be violent, so can an iced tea. The First Amendment protects speech on hats; it does NOT protect businesses open to the public to discriminate against its customers because they're Jews while chasing them in the street shouting 'Jew' at them.

HAMAS, HEZBOLLAH FLAGS FLY AT ANTI-ISRAEL PROTEST MINUTES AFTER MAMDANI CONDEMNS TERROR PLOT AGAINST JEWS

"On the one-year anniversary of October 7th, a Palestinian terrorist attack against innocent civilians that killed over 1,200 people and took hundreds of hostages including children and Americans, Jerusalem Coffee Shop in Oakland unveiled a new menu celebrating terrorism. Beverage items named 'Iced in Tea Fada' celebrate Intifada (an Arabic call to violence signifying resistance by any means necessary, including terrorism) and 'Sweet Sinwar' honoring the principal architect behind the attack," she added.

The coffee shop co-founder previously denied that "Sweet Sinwar" referred to the Hamas leader and said the menu's Oct. 7 rollout coincided with the business's anniversary rather than the anniversary of the Hamas attack, according to The San Francisco Standard.

Barcohana said she hoped the current shutdown would become permanent.

FBI NABS 7 FOR ALLEGED 'CAMPAIGN OF VIOLENCE' TO PRESSURE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN, BUSINESSES OVER ISRAEL TIES

"The owners have temporarily closed the coffee shop while they defend this discrimination lawsuit against them," she said. "Hopefully it remains permanently closed."

The Justice Department filed its case in June 2025 under Title II of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. 

The Anti-Defamation League and Benesch sued on behalf of Michael Radice, who alleges he was refused service and subjected to antisemitic slurs, while the Louis D. Brandeis Center filed a state lawsuit on behalf of Jonathan Hirsch, who was ejected with his young son after Harara confronted him over his Star of David hat.

When the Justice Department announced its case, Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Civil Rights Division said federal public-accommodation laws applied regardless of the business's political views.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"It is illegal, intolerable and reprehensible for any American business open to the public to refuse to serve Jewish customers," she said. "Through our vigorous enforcement of Title II of the Civil Rights Act and other laws prohibiting race and religious discrimination, the Justice Department is committed to combatting antisemitism and discrimination and protecting the civil rights of all Americans."

Fox News Digital reached out to Jerusalem Coffee House and the DOJ for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Youth football coaches fighting & acting like fools in Pennsylvania isn't the least bit shocking

item.content:encoded:
After a summer in which a travel baseball pitcher was allegedly ordered by his father to throw at the opposing team's dugout in what was a very troubling incident, we shouldn't be shocked in the least about what happened at a Pennsylvania youth football game.

During Saturday's game in western Pennsylvania, youth coach Dequay Canton of the Carlynton Little Cougars was seen enraged and fighting coaches from Keystone Oaks. In a statement, Canton claimed he was being portrayed by the national media to be the aggressor, but he says racism is what fueled his actions.

LAWSUIT ALLEGES SOCCER COACH BENCHED TEEN WHO WAS INJURED BY TEAMMATE FOR ALLEGED RACIAL SLUR

Without providing evidence, Canton claimed "our black and brown kids continued to be called an 'N,' and every quarter our kids were called the 'N' word, and we addressed it with the referees, but there was no response."

He continued, "It's a shame that in 2026, 8-9-year-old kids are calling young black and brown kids the 'N.' It's even more shameful that their parents, coaches and referees let them do it without correcting them. They would rather fight me for addressing it than correct their kids. That should be the story. Period."

The Carlynton youth football team followed up Canton's statement by announcing that the man who recorded the incident, Ryan Crux, has been banned from team football events. Crux's son plays for the Carlynton team. Crux admitted to Pittsburgh media Tuesday night that there was bad blood brewing between him and the coaching staff. It turns out, this video probably helped facilitate a ban.

"My son has been getting screamed at things like 'go get that f–kin ball!' since he was 6 years old. I don't speak to my son like that and I don't want anyone else speaking to him like that," Crux wrote on Facebook this week. "Now hes 9 years old talking like hes 15 and I blame it all on youth football coaches. I don't want to hear him speak like that but hes been hearing it from these wack ass coaches for 3 years straight so what f–kin difference does it make now?"

YOUTH SOFTBALL COACH & UMPIRE GET INTO UGLY CONFRONTATION AS EMOTIONS BOIL OVER AT ARKANSAS TOURNAMENT

By now, none of this should be shocking. It's business as usual in a world where mom and dad are blowing $260 a weekend to attend travel basketball tournaments. It's a world where 11U pitchers are allegedly told to throw a fastball at his opponent's dugout –– and then the boy obeyed the alleged orders.

It's a world where a Mississippi sheriff lost his job this summer for fighting an umpire after a 14U travel baseball game. It's also a world where a parent is willing to come out on the field to trip a kid who's running towards the end zone.

YOUTH PITCHER LAUNCHES FASTBALL AT OPPOSING DUGOUT AFTER ALLEGED ORDER FROM COACH: 'ABSOLUTELY BUSH LEAGUE'

It's also a world where, just this week in Ohio, 11 members of a top Cleveland high school football team were charged with theft after ripping off $4,500 in merchandise from a Columbus Dick's while in town for a football game. Two of those charged with the thefts are adults, including one who had committed to a scholarship from D-1 Kent State.

Who's to blame? All of us. Americans have actively destroyed community youth sports for so long that there's no putting the genie back in the bottle at this point. We've created life-or-death 8-9U football leagues with parents who are ready to battle the second they leave their SUVs.

We've put people like Dequay Canton in charge of our kids and let him run wild.

Do Americans have the spine to do better? Apparently not. These incidents keep happening and show no sign of slowing down.

item.title: Naomi Osaka's latest over-the-top US Open outfit is a tribute to 76ers star Allen Iverson
item.description: Naomi Osaka cosplayed as Allen Iverson at the 2026 US Open, but the NBA Hall of Famer never played in New York and was never a Nike athlete.
item.content:encoded:
Naomi Osaka treating the entrance tunnel at Grand Slams like it's the red carpet at the Met Gala is nothing new. The four-time Slam winner has worn some very memorable outfits in years past, but her wardrobe choice at the 2026 US Open may take the crown as her most out-of-left-field to date.

Making her way onto the court inside Arthur Ashe Stadium on Monday for her first-round match, the Japanese star wore a short-sleeved hoodie, red and black arm sleeves, and a full-length skirt. After eventually taking off her hood, she revealed she was wearing a black headband and had her hair done in cornrows.

It turns out that she was cosplaying as NBA legend and Hall of Famer Allen Iverson.

FROM COLIN KAEPERNICK TO DYLAN MULVANEY, NIKE'S DECADE OF LEFT-WING ACTIVISM HAS FINALLY CAUGHT UP TO IT

"It’s my, I guess, my tribute to Iverson. I really like him a lot," Osaka said after her first-round victory. "I mean, Nike said basketball, so I said: ‘Okay, you want basketball, I’ll give you basketball.’"

Nike going with a basketball theme for some of its athletes at this year's US Open in New York makes at least a bit of sense with the Knicks winning their first NBA title since 1973 back in June. World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka wore an orange dress at the tournament, clearly paying homage to one of the Knicks' colors.

Osaka tipping her cap to Iverson, however, makes absolutely zero sense for a plethora of different reasons.

For starters, Iverson never played for a New York franchise during his NBA career. He played collegiately at Georgetown in Washington, D.C., and originally hails from the state of Virginia. Iverson spent the bulk of his career playing for the Philadelphia 76ers, a rival to the Knicks.

If you think Osaka is simply paying homage to one of the great Nike athletes of all time, well, you'd be wrong there, too.

Iverson was never a Nike athlete. After being selected by the 76ers first overall in the 1996 NBA Draft, Iverson inked an endorsement deal with Reebok. Iverson and Reebok went on to create an iconic signature shoe, and the 11-time All-Star later signed a lifetime endorsement deal with the brand.

Osaka deciding to pay tribute to Iverson during a Grand Slam in New York City is about as baffling as her designing and wearing an outfit inspired by a jellyfish in a children's book, which is exactly what she did at this year's Australian Open.

item.title: Fans react to six NHL teams jumping to Prime Video for in-market streaming Including Stanley Cup champs
item.description: Six NHL teams, including the Carolina Hurricanes, are moving local games to Amazon Prime Video, but confusing subscription tiers await fans.
item.content:encoded:
There's never been a weirder time to watch sports on TV, and that's thanks to the fall of regional sports networks and the rise of streaming.

Now, six NHL teams have announced that, for fans in their market, their games will be streamed on Amazon's Prime Video.

The news was made official on Wednesday with the Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes, Anaheim Ducks, Columbus Blue Jackets, Dallas Stars, Minnesota Wild, and St. Louis Blues all moving over to the platform for local fans.

BROADCASTERS URGE CONGRESS TO REEXAMINE SPORTS BROADCASTING ACT AS GAMES SHIFT TO STREAMING PAYWALLS

But because this is the age of streaming, it's still going to be a little confusing and potentially costly.

The league said that individual teams will release information about packages and subscriptions. Strangely, it appears that some teams will be available to fans as an add-on on top of their Prime Video membership, some can be purchased without a Prime Video subscription, and some will be included with the standard membership.

WATCHING THE NFL WILL COST MORE, REQUIRE MORE STREAMING SERVICES THAN EVER THIS SEASON

But it still gets more confusing: most of the teams making the move are still going to offer some kind of alternative to streaming.

Then, of course, as per usual, if the game happens to be one that's televised nationally by TNT, ESPN, or ABC, that one will not be available for you to stream on Prime Video.

It's always nice to have options, but there's no doubt that a lot of fans are getting fed up with having to add another streaming platform, and in some cases, an additional add-on on top of that, to their laundry list of channels and streamers needed to watch their favorite teams.

There's certainly a sense of streaming fatigue for a lot of fans, especially as more and more clubs move away from regional sports networks.

Of course, these services are only for fans in those teams' markets. The streaming rights for out-of-market games in the US still belong to ESPN+, as they have for several years.
